headline: Discussed scam prevention, senior emergency shelter options, and concerns about Greater Springfield Senior Services; no votes recorded.
summary: Police Detective Gregory McCain described current scams targeting older adults and advised residents to verify callers and not respond to suspicious messages. Discussion also covered concerns about referrals, coordination with Greater Springfield Senior Services, and cold-weather shelter options. Planned follow-up includes a November 17 presentation at the Raymond Jordan Senior Center; no votes were recorded.

Public Portion 
 1. Senior Scams 
 2. Constituent concerns regarding Greater Springfield Senior Services. 
 
Minutes: 
On October 1, 2026, the Elder Affairs Committee, chaired by Councilor Kateri Walsh, met to 
discuss scams affecting older adults and related safety concerns. Springfield Police Detective 
Gregory McCain provided information on current scams, including fraudulent phone calls and 
text messages, phishing, bank and tax scams, romance scams, false warrant demands, and 
individuals falsely representing utility or service companies. McCain advised residents not to 
respond to suspicious calls or messages, to independently verify the identity of callers or visitors, 
and to contact police when suspicious individuals appear at their homes. 
 
The committee also discussed concerns regarding services and emergency assistance for older 
adults. Detective McCain reported difficulties obtaining follow-up information regarding 
referrals involving older adults and raised concerns about coordination with Greater Springfield 
Senior Services. The committee discussed the need to clarify the agency's response protocols and 
coordination with the Police Department. Additional discussion addressed cold-weather 
assistance and appropriate emergency shelter options for older adults, including possible 
coordination with City departments, community organizations, churches, and other facilities. 
 
Follow-up will include continued scam-prevention education and outreach, including a 
November 17 presentation at the Raymond Jordan Senior Center and additional presentations by 
Detective McCain as requested. The committee will also follow up on emergency assistance and 
shelter options for older adults and seek a future meeting with Greater Springfield Senior 
Services to discuss its response protocols and coordination with the City and Police Department. 
The committee will continue reviewing these matters at a future meeting.  
 
The meeting adjourned at 2:00 p.m.
